author: janleike
text:
@chasebrignac LLMs are pretty different from any kind of software we've written before; they are much more general and much more capable at the same time.

Seems good to worry about regulatory capture but this bill is not it.

author: janleike
text:
Many companies are currently on track to build superhuman AI systems, and we don't yet know how to make them reliably safe (figuring this out has been my job for approx. the last decade).

More regulation will be needed as we learn more about AI, but SB 1047 is a decent start.

author: janleike
text: If your model causes mass casualties or >$500 million in damages, something has clearly gone very wrong. Such a scenario is not a normal part of innovation.

author: janleike
text:
I call upon Governor @GavinNewsom to not veto SB 1047.

The bill is a meaningful step forward for AI safety regulation, with no better alternatives in sight.

author: janleike
text:
We use a multi-agent training setup where an honest prover and a sneaky prover write solutions checked by a small model.

The honest prover wants to convince the small model of a correct solution, while the sneaky prover tries to fool it with a flawed solution.

author: janleike

author: janleike
text:
To all OpenAI employees, I want to say:

Learn to feel the AGI.

Act with the gravitas appropriate for what you're building.

I believe you can "ship" the cultural change that's needed.

I am counting on you.

The world is counting on you.

:openai-heart:

author: janleike
text: OpenAI must become a safety-first AGI company.

author: janleike
text:
We are long overdue in getting incredibly serious about the implications of AGI.

We must prioritize preparing for them as best we can.

Only then can we ensure AGI benefits all of humanity.

author: janleike
text: But over the past years, safety culture and processes have taken a backseat to shiny products.

author: janleike
text:
Building smarter-than-human machines is an inherently dangerous endeavor.

OpenAI is shouldering an enormous responsibility on behalf of all of humanity.

author: janleike
text: Over the past few months my team has been sailing against the wind. Sometimes we were struggling for compute and it was getting harder and harder to get this crucial research done.

author: janleike
text: These problems are quite hard to get right, and I am concerned we aren't on a trajectory to get there.

author: janleike
text: I believe much more of our bandwidth should be spent getting ready for the next generations of models, on security, monitoring, preparedness, safety, adversarial robustness, (super)alignment, confidentiality, societal impact, and related topics.

author: janleike
text:
I joined because I thought OpenAI would be the best place in the world to do this research.

However, I have been disagreeing with OpenAI leadership about the company's core priorities for quite some time, until we finally reached a breaking point.

author: janleike
text: Stepping away from this job has been one of the hardest things I have ever done, because we urgently need to figure out how to steer and control AI systems much smarter than us.

author: janleike
text:
I love my team.

I'm so grateful for the many amazing people I got to work with, both inside and outside of the superalignment team.

OpenAI has so much exceptionally smart, kind, and effective talent.

author: janleike
text: It's been such a wild journey over the past ~3 years. My team launched the first ever RLHF LLM with InstructGPT, published the first scalable oversight on LLMs, pioneered automated interpretability and weak-to-strong generalization. More exciting stuff is coming out soon.

author: janleike
text: Yesterday was my last day as head of alignment, superalignment lead, and executive @OpenAI.

author: janleike
text:
It supports both neurons and attention heads.

You can intervene on the forward pass by ablating individual neurons and see what changes.

In short, it's a quick and easy way to discover circuits manually.

author: janleike
text:
Today we're releasing a tool we've been using internally to analyze transformer internals - the Transformer Debugger!

It combines both automated interpretability and sparse autoencoders, and it allows rapid exploration of models without writing code.
